Bond Topology & Complexes¶

The snap_analyze.analyze module provides utility functions for filtering bonds, extracting connected particle clusters (complexes) using graph theoretical algorithms, and cleaning intermediate bond nodes.

Module Reference¶

Module for bond manipulation, topology splitting, and connected complex graph analysis.

snap_analyze.analyze.convert_id_to_complex_id(particle_ids, complex_IDs)[source]¶

Map particle indices to their corresponding complex IDs.

Parameters:

  • particle_ids (array_like) – Particle indices to look up.

  • complex_IDs (array_like) – Array mapping particle index -> complex ID.

Returns:

complex_ids – Complex IDs corresponding to the given particle indices.

Return type:

ndarray

snap_analyze.analyze.convert_id_to_type(particle_ids, particle_types)[source]¶

Map particle indices to their corresponding particle types.

Parameters:

  • particle_ids (array_like) – Particle indices to look up.

  • particle_types (array_like) – Array mapping particle index -> particle type.

Returns:

types – Particle types corresponding to the given particle indices.

Return type:

ndarray

snap_analyze.analyze.get_complexes(num_particles, particle_typeIDs, bond_groups, return_type_info=False)[source]¶

Identify connected clusters (complexes) of bonded particles using graph analysis.

Parameters:

  • num_particles (int) – Total number of particles in the system.

  • particle_typeIDs (array_like) – Array of shape (num_particles,) containing particle type IDs.

  • bond_groups (array_like) – Array of shape (N_bonds, 2) containing particle index pairs defining bonds.

  • return_type_info (bool, optional) – If True, returns additional complex classification type IDs and ordered unique types. Default is False.

Returns:

  • comp_IDs (ndarray) – Array of length num_particles mapping each particle index to its assigned complex ID.

  • type_info (tuple of (ndarray, list), optional) – Only returned if return_type_info is True. Tuple containing: - comp_typeIDs: Array mapping each complex to its complex-type ID. - ordered_comp_types: List of unique particle-type tuples defining each complex type.

snap_analyze.analyze.remove_bond_intermediates(bond_groups, particle_typeIDs, to_remove, return_removed_bonds=False)[source]¶

Remove specified intermediate particle types from bond graphs, connecting remaining endpoints directly.

Parameters:

  • bond_groups (array_like) – Array of shape (N_bonds, 2) defining existing bonds.

  • particle_typeIDs (array_like) – Array of shape (num_particles,) containing particle type IDs.

  • to_remove (int or iterable of int) – Particle type ID(s) to remove from the bond network.

  • return_removed_bonds (bool, optional) – If True, also returns a dictionary detailing removed intermediate bond connections. Default is False.

Returns:

  • ret_bonds (ndarray) – Updated bond index pairs after removing intermediate particles.

  • removed_bonds_dict (dict, optional) – Returned only if return_removed_bonds is True.

snap_analyze.analyze.split_static_dyn_bonds(bond_groups, bond_typeIDs, dyn_bond_types)[source]¶

Split bond indices into static and dynamic bond subsets based on bond types.

Parameters:

  • bond_groups (array_like) – Array of shape (N_bonds, 2) containing particle index pairs defining each bond.

  • bond_typeIDs (array_like) – Array of shape (N_bonds,) containing type integer IDs for each bond.

  • dyn_bond_types (array_like or iterable) – Type integer IDs considered to be dynamic bonds.

Returns:

  • stat_bonds (ndarray) – Bond particle pairs belonging to static bond types.

  • dyn_bonds (ndarray) – Bond particle pairs belonging to dynamic bond types.
